guide_faq_uttrykk_a: An uttrykk (Norwegian for "expression") is a fixed phrase you learn as a whole, not word by word. There are three kinds: idioms, whose meaning isn't in the words (ha is i magen means to stay calm); ordtak, or proverbs (Morgenstund har gull i munn); and everyday formulas such as greetings, polite phrases and set sentences (god morgen, vær så snill). Single words, and fixed phrases that work like one word (i går, ved siden av), count as vocabulary instead.

guide_page_subtitle: Norskeord is a vocabulary app built for serious Norwegian learners.
guide_scheduling_1: After flipping a card, rate how well you remembered it — Again, Hard, Good, or Easy. The app uses that to decide when to show it again.
guide_scheduling_2: Words you find easy come back less often. Words you forget come back sooner. Over time it builds a personal schedule for each word.
guide_scheduling_3: A card's schedule strengthens with each review, so a familiar card and a brand-new one can get different intervals even for the same rating.
guide_scheduling_4: Rate honestly — tapping Easy on something you're unsure about removes it from your deck for a long time.
guide_scheduling_5: Want reviews spaced closer together or further apart overall? Adjust it in Profile → Preferences → Review intensity.
guide_buttons_intro: Ask yourself: how easy was it to recall that word?
guide_btn_again_desc: Couldn't recall it. Card returns later in the same session.
guide_btn_hard_desc: Got it, but slowly or with effort. Short interval increase.
guide_btn_good_desc: Recalled correctly with normal effort. Use this most of the time.
guide_btn_easy_desc: Instantly obvious. Next review jumps far into the future — use sparingly.
guide_state_new_desc: You have not seen this word yet.
guide_state_learning_desc: You have seen this word but it has not settled into long-term memory yet. Keep rating it and it will graduate soon.
guide_state_memorized_desc: This word has moved into long-term memory. It will come back for review occasionally to keep it fresh.
guide_state_forgotten_desc: You rated this word Again after it was memorized. It is back in practice and will come back more frequently until it sticks again.
guide_plus_tip: Plus tip: Norskeord Plus builds a personal Due today deck from your ratings — a short, focused session of only the words your memory needs right now.
guide_faq_reminder_q: What is the daily study reminder?
guide_faq_reminder_a: A browser push notification sent once a day to remind you to study. To enable it, go to Profile → Notifications → Daily study reminder. Your browser will ask for permission the first time.
guide_faq_no_reminder_q: I enabled the reminder but nothing arrives. Why?
guide_faq_no_reminder_a: Check that your browser is allowed to send notifications in your OS settings (System Settings → Notifications). On iPhone, notifications only work if you have added Norskeord to your home screen first (Share → Add to Home Screen).
guide_faq_sync_q: My progress isn't showing on my other device.
guide_faq_sync_a: Progress syncs across devices for Plus members. Free accounts store progress on the current device only.
guide_faq_offline_a: Yes. Install it as an app (Share → Add to Home Screen on iPhone, or the install prompt in Chrome) and flashcard decks you have opened before will work without an internet connection. Ratings are saved locally and sync when you reconnect.
guide_faq_freeplus_q: What is the difference between Free and Plus?
guide_faq_prefs_q: How do I change my flashcard preferences?
guide_faq_prefs_a: Go to Profile → Preferences. You can set your level, interface language, flashcard direction, card type, pronunciation speed, and cards per session.
guide_faq_intensity_a: It shifts how far apart all your reviews are spaced. Relaxed reviews less often, Intensive reviews more often, for stronger retention. Change it in Profile → Preferences.
guide_faq_download_q: How do I download my progress report?
guide_faq_download_a: Go to Profile → Account and click Download Progress report. This exports all your card history as a file you can save or share.

guide_start_intro: Norskeord has four learning modes. Here's a quick guide to which one fits your goal right now:
guide_start_path_beginner_desc: Start with A1 flashcards — everyday words with audio on every card.
guide_start_path_exam_desc: Go straight to the exam prep section, organised by the topics that appear on the test.
guide_start_path_quiz_desc: Quiz mode asks you to recall words actively, not just flip cards.
guide_start_path_grammar_desc: Grammar practice covers word order, ikke-placement, and more.
guide_start_note: All four modes update your review schedule — so your flashcards, quiz, and grammar practice share the same progress.
guide_flashcards_intro: Every card has audio. Switch direction anytime: Norwegian → English, English → Norwegian, or Definition → Norwegian. Rate each card after flipping.
guide_quiz_intro: Quiz mode tests active recall — you have to produce or recognise an answer, not just flip a card. There are three question types:
guide_quiz_mc: Multiple choice — pick the correct translation from four options. Press A B C D on keyboard.
guide_quiz_fill: Fill in the blank — complete a sentence with the missing Norwegian word.
guide_quiz_type: Typed answer — type the Norwegian word for an English prompt from memory.
guide_quiz_scheduling: Every quiz answer updates your review schedule, just like flashcard ratings.
guide_quiz_access: Free: all of A1, plus 3 categories at each higher level. Plus: all categories across all levels.
guide_grammar_intro: Grammar practice focuses on the structural rules of Norwegian that vocabulary alone cannot teach. Topics are organised by CEFR level and cover:
guide_grammar_type_fill: Fill in the blank — supply the correct form of a word in context.
guide_grammar_type_order: Word order — arrange words into a grammatically correct Norwegian sentence.
guide_grammar_type_transform: Transform — rewrite a sentence following a rule (e.g. negation, tense change).
guide_grammar_rule: After each answer, you see the grammar rule that explains why — with an optional deeper read if you want the full explanation.
guide_grammar_access: Free: A1 grammar topics. Plus: all topics including advanced sentence transformations.
guide_norskproven_what: Norskprøven is the official Norwegian exam, required for residency and citizenship. Norskeord covers it with exam-topic vocabulary decks and full practice tests.
guide_norskproven_how: Practice tests are exam-style tasks at A2 and B1 level, in three formats:
guide_norskproven_reading: Reading — short passages with multiple-choice comprehension questions.
guide_norskproven_writing: Writing — structured prompts with model answers so you can compare your response.
guide_norskproven_oral: Oral — role-play scenarios and discussion questions with a built-in 2-minute preparation timer.
guide_norskproven_access: Free: Practice Test 1 at A2 and B1. Plus: all practice tests.
guide_lang_intro: Norskeord has two separate language settings. The interface language (set in Profile → Preferences) controls the menus, labels, and text throughout the app — you can use it in English, Spanish, or Ukrainian.
guide_lang_change: The flashcard language controls what the back of each card shows — the translation you see after flipping. This is also set in Profile → Preferences and can be changed independently of the interface language.
guide_faq_freeplus_a_v2: Free covers all of A1 (vocabulary, phrases, quiz and grammar) and 3 vocabulary and quiz categories at each level from A2 to C. Plus unlocks everything: all levels, smart scheduling, cross-device sync, all quiz and grammar topics, Norskprøven practice tests, and full-text search. See the full comparison:

guide_faq_norskproven_a: The official Norwegian exam required for residency and citizenship. The prep section covers vocabulary and practice tests at A2 and B1.
